instructions: Finely chop the onions. Mince the garlic and grate 1 tbsp of the ginger. Rinse the lentils in a strainer until the water runs mostly clear.

Heat the oil in a medium pot over medium heat. Add the onions, 1/4 cup water and 1/4 tsp of the salt. Cook for 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until the onions are soft and starting to turn golden. Add a splash of water if they start to stick.
Add the garlic, ginger and turmeric. Stir for 1 minute, until it smells fragrant.
Add the lentils and 4 1/2 cups of water, and bring to a boil. Skim off any foam.
Turn the heat to low and simmer, stirring every few minutes, for 20 to 25 minutes, until the lentils have broken down into a thick, soft stew. Add a splash of water if it gets too thick.
Meanwhile, rinse the rice and cook it according to the package.
Stir in the remaining 1 tsp salt and the pepper. Cook for 2 minutes.
Slice the jalapeño into rings and put them in a small bowl for anyone who wants heat.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Serve with the rice or with injera, and the jalapeño on the table.
method_notes: No version I could read showed a rating, so this is a fallback lead: the Food.com mild split lentil stew (yemser alicha), a Yewoin family recipe, cooks onion in oil and water, adds garlic, ginger and turmeric, and finishes with a green pepper. Luladey Moges's misir wot (CBC) uses 1 cup of lentils to 1 cup of water and swaps 1 tsp of turmeric in for the berbere. I used the turmeric amount from Moges, a thicker lentil to water ratio than the lead, a smaller amount of ginger, black pepper in place of white, and the green pepper on the side so it stays kid friendly.
